title: A Safety Case Per Robot Type: Starting Hazards for a Ground Vehicle, an Arm and a Legged Robot, and a Checker That Refuses a Case With a Hole in It

questions.question: What makes a safety claim worth anything?
options: The number of hazards it lists
A statement that the robot was tested
questions.explanation: Every hazard has a control, and every control has a test. A case is a table that can be checked: no hazard without a control, no control without a test that passes.

questions.question: How many hazards did the template of the ground vehicle start with?
questions.explanation: A collision with a person, a runaway, tipping, a slope, the battery, a trapped limb, a lost position and motion during maintenance.

questions.question: The empty ground template had how many problems?
options: 0: an empty case has nothing wrong
questions.explanation: Every hazard lacked a control and a stated residual risk, which is two holes each.

questions.question: Why is a control with no test a hole?
options: Nothing shows that it works: it is a hope
questions.explanation: A control whose test does not pass is a known failure, and one with no test has never been tried.

questions.question: Why is a high risk controlled only by a sign refused?
options: A sign is not a control at all
Information relies on a person doing the right thing, and a high risk needs a function that does not
questions.explanation: A sign works only if someone reads and obeys it. For a high risk the case needs a design change or a safety function.

questions.question: Does a case with no holes mean the robot is safe?
options: No: it means the table has none, and the review and the hardware still have to say the rest
Yes, for the hazards in the template
questions.explanation: The checker reads a table. Whether the hazards are the right ones, and whether the robot behaves as the tests say, is for a review and the hardware.
